text:
alice.m: quick heads up — noticed a weird latency hump on H100s this morning when the KV cache is cold and seq_len ~128. p50 fine, p95 up ~2.3x, p99 spikes. traced it to repeated Triton->CUTLASS switchovers under load.

ben.k: any chance this is batch-smearing from the new autoscaler?

alice.m: looked at queuing, not classic smearing. traces show kernel-router probing every ~30s and flipping when probe sample sees slightly higher throughput on CUTLASS; then next probe flips back. basically flip-flop.

carla.s: saw similar in canary last night. attaching profiler snippet: 
```
# probe log excerpt
time=2026-03-17T08:23:12Z probe_id=37 seq=128 backend=triton latency_ms=19.2
time=2026-03-17T08:23:44Z probe_id=38 seq=128 backend=cutlass latency_ms=17.6
time=2026-03-17T08:24:05Z router=decide backend=cutlass p99_ms=145.9
time=2026-03-17T08:24:35Z router=decide backend=triton p99_ms=310.2 # huge
```

dinesh.g: curious — is KV hit-rate correlated? if kv-hit is low it tends to enlarge effective seq (more memcpy/kvcost) which can tilt kernel preference.

alice.m: yes — on the affected shard kv-hit ~12% during ramp; when hit-rate dips below ~20% our perf model shifts preference to triton for small batches, but runtime probe sometimes mistakes transient noise for signal.

ben.k: so root cause = aggressive probe cadence + no stickiness window. router oscillates because the net perf difference is within noise band.

carla.s: right. also noticed the sampling population is tiny for seq128 — only ~8 probe samples per minute due to prioritized traffic routing; sample variance is big.

eva.t: proposal: add a probe cooldown and a weighted moving average with count-based confidence. e.g. require N samples and 30s cooldown after a decision; also bias toward current path unless new path shows >X% improvement with CI. pseudo-config: 
```
router.probe:
  min_samples: 20
  cooldown_s: 45
  ci_threshold_pct: 7.5
  prefer_stable_bias: 0.6  # weight current path
```

alice.m: also propose tying decision to kv-hit fold: if kv-hit < 25% treat seq_len as +1 bucket (so prefer kernels optimized for higher effective seq). avoids ping-pong when cold.

dinesh.g: 👍 that makes sense. we should also avoid probing during autoscaler transient windows (scale-up/scale-down). skip probes for 60s after any scaling event.

ben.k: can we run a synthetic that replays seq128 traffic with kv-hit toggles? want to verify no regressions for steady-state.

carla.s: i can run replay on canary cluster. plan: 30m baseline (current router), 30m experiment (cooldown+bias), measure p50/p95/p99 and route flip count.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by carla.s -> env=canary cluster=eu-west-1 change=router.probe.config ref=diff-PR-8142

eva.t: when you run it, please capture per-backend tail CPU/GPU utilization + NVTX spans around the kernel choice so we know if CUTLASS wins but costs more GPU time.

carla.s: will do. assigning: carla -> run replay + collect traces, alice -> add kv-hit fold to runtime heuristic, dinesh -> add autoscale-skip, eva -> update decision logic config and rollout plan.

alice.m: one more: add metric `router.flip_rate` and alert if flips/sec > 0.2 for >5m. helps catch regressions.

ben.k: sweet. timeline?

carla.s: starting run in ~45m, will post results here. if successful we'll roll to dedicated on Mon.

alice.m: thanks team. @eva.t can you draft a short blurb for release notes explaining the probe cooldown and kv-aware routing? :thumbsup:

eva.t: on it.

carla.s: test started 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z; will update after 30m.

ben.k: appreciate the quick triage.

alice.m: added TODO in runtime repo: `router/docs: explain sample sizing and kv-hit fold`

carla.s: TL;DR after 30m: flip_rate dropped from 0.9->0.04 flips/min, p99 for seq128 dropped from 310ms->142ms, no CPU/GPU cost regression observed. posting full traces next.
